newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai Soybean futures ended mixed on Tuesday with investors uncertain about the short-term market trend, traders said.
The most active November 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,325 yuan ($401) per tonne, rising 23 yuan. It opened at 3,300 and hit a low of 3,296.
July fell two yuan to 3,250, September rose eight to 3,318, the January 1998 contract fell 39 to 3,272 and March rose 114 to 3,330.
Combined volume rose to 15,900 tonnes from 15,500.
Soybean opened mostly lower but speculative buying pushed the prices up to end at their intra-day highs.
Traders said market uncertainties made investors stay on the sidelines but speculative buying was active at low levels.

"Many speculators were interested in buying below the 3,300-yuan level today because they believe soybean prices will not drift far away from that level," one trader said. "But they are likely to liquidate their long positions in the next few days once prices increase."
Traders said they expected soybean to move around the 3,300-yuan level in the short term. ($1 =8.2925 yuan)
